lines: ## Medicaid VBC Expansion Business Case

Medicaid is the highest-cost, highest-utilization LOB with zero VBC attribution. This page quantifies the financial and clinical opportunity of bringing 12,500 Medicaid members under value-based care management.
### Medicaid vs All LOBs — Why Medicaid Is the Highest-Impact Target
### Medicaid Cost & Utilization Trends — Deteriorating Without Intervention
### Medicaid Member Profile — Risk, Cost, and Care Gap Landscape
### Medicaid Quality Gaps — HEDIS Measures Driving Star Ratings

### Executive Summary

**The case for Medicaid VBC expansion is clear:** 12,500 members with 0% VBC attribution, a 106.8% MLR (claims exceed premium by $16.1M in avoidable spend), 220/1K ED rate (highest across all LOBs), and 14.4% readmission rate. MA's VBC program demonstrates the model works — extending attribution to Medicaid could capture a significant share of the $16.1M avoidable spend through care management, ED diversion, and readmission reduction programs. Priority actions: (1) Identify 2–3 ACOs with Medicaid managed care experience, (2) Pilot shared savings contracts targeting the 1,262 high-cost members first, (3) Deploy NBA-driven outreach to close care gaps.
## Commercial VBC Expansion Business Case

Commercial is the largest LOB by membership (20,000 members) with zero VBC attribution and $14.1M in avoidable spend. Unlike Medicaid, Commercial operates at a healthy 86% MLR — the opportunity here is margin protection and employer retention through proactive utilization management.

lines:
### Executive Summary

**The Commercial VBC case is a margin-protection play, not a loss-recovery story.** At 86% MLR, Commercial is profitable — but $14.1M in avoidable spend represents ~9% of total claims that erode employer satisfaction and renewal rates. With 20,000 members (the largest LOB), 2,090 high-cost members, and the lowest ED rate at 102/1K, the Commercial population is structurally healthier but still carries preventable utilization. The readmission rate (12.3%) is already best-in-class, but avoidable spend share (~9.1%) matches MA — meaning proportional waste is equivalent despite lower overall cost. Priority actions: (1) Partner with employer-focused ACOs or CINs on bundled payment pilots for the 2,090 high-cost members, (2) Deploy preventive care NBA outreach to the 6,300+ members with active recommendations, (3) Structure gainsharing incentives around avoidable ED/IP reduction to protect employer-group margins.
